To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of abnormal signal in the posterior limb on the internal capsule (a sign of injury to the brain) predicts that the baby is at high risk of developing a neurodisability (abnormal development of the nervous system).
abnormal magnetic resonance signal intensity in the internal capsule on cranial magnetic resonance scans of term infants with hypoxic ischemic encephalitis predicts a poor neurodevelopmental outcome.

abnormal signal intensity in a region of the brain called the posterior limb of internal capsule on a brain scan predicts a poor neurodevelopmental outcome (ie, a poor score on a test of neurodevelopmental function) at one year of age in a group of term neonates with a brain disorder called hypoxic-ischemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of magnetic resonance (MR) in the prediction of neurodevelopmental impairment in infants with hypoxia-ischaemia.
the development of a novel method of assessing the severity of brain injury in infants with hypoxia ischemia.
the use of magnetic resonance imaging to predict the outcome for term infants with hypoxic ischemic encephalopathies (HIE) and to assess the potential for neuroprotection by hypothermia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a normal signal intensity in the internal capsule on magnetic resonance imaging in infants with HIE is associated with a normal neurodevelopmental outcome, but the presence of an abnormal signal in the internal capsule is associated with a poor neurodevelopmental outcome.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PLIC signal intensity can be used as an early indicator of outcome and that the PLIC should be routinely imaged when evaluating infants with HIE.
the presence of a signal abnormality in the posterior limb is an excellent indicator of a poor neurodevelopmental outcome.

The main takeaway from our work is that
abnormal magnetic resonance imaging in the PLIC predicts poor neurodevelopmental outcome.
abnormal signal intensity in this region of the brain predicts neurodevelopmental impairment.
